elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty covers only conformance "in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement"; no professional-and-workmanlike (or industry-standard) warranty was added, and Section 11 remains a bare standard-of-care covenant, not a warranty.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery or performance" for the software; the preferred twelve-month period was expressly not pressed.
The 90-day period applies to both the software and "the Hosting Services and Support Services".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services".
Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 9 covers only Year 2000 date handling.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code or virus warranty is present in the rendered text.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery or performance, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — 90 days meets the floor; the deterministic period check is a false negative because the operative text does state "ninety (90) days".

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The same 90-day period covers "the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement", exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services" at Vendor's option, consistent with the model language.
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: a 90-day conformance warranty for the software (against documentation) and for the Hosting and Support Services, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund of fees paid.

Preferred level is incomplete: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, and there is no professional-and-workmanlike warranty, no compliance-with-laws warranty and no malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred the drafter would need to extend the software period to twelve (12) months and add those three warranty limbs.

The deterministic 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' check reports not ok, but substantive inspection of the operative sentence shows an express "period of ninety (90) days following delivery or performance", which satisfies the fallback floor; treat the regex result as a false negative rather than a defect.

Minimal: a single inserted warranty sentence plus one remedy sentence, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no notice procedure and no extra damages or indemnity content beyond the fallback checklist. Existing favourable language (the Year 2000 warranty, Section 11 standard of care, and the pre-existing "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" carve-out) is retained unchanged, so no separate disclaimer carve-out edit was needed.

Preserves intent: the insertion introduces no undefined terms (Hosting Services is defined in Section 3; Support Services is already used in the retained Section 9 text), creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained disclaimer, which by its own opening words yields to express warranties.
